screenshots.title: Open the Pomade workspace
screenshots.caption: The usdGen > Pomade workspace opens with the Bind scalp mesh button and a first-run hint; grooming modes are gated until a scalp is bound.
screenshots.ui: usdGen > Pomade > Open workspace

screenshots.title: Bind the scalp mesh
screenshots.caption: Bind scalp mesh selected /Scalp; Graph and Create region are now active in the dock.
screenshots.ui: Bind scalp mesh...; Graph > Create region

screenshots.title: Close the first region
screenshots.caption: Three clicks and Enter close the first triangular region on /Scalp; the exercise intentionally leaves part of the scalp uncovered.
screenshots.ui: Graph > Create region; Enter

screenshots.title: Two closed regions
screenshots.caption: The second region closes by clicking its first CV. The two partial-coverage regions have committed and the dock reports Synced.
screenshots.ui: Graph > Create region; Synced

screenshots.title: Select a tube
screenshots.caption: Tube mode and Whole tube component selection are active; clicking the tube wall selects the tube and exposes its transform controls.
screenshots.ui: Tube > Whole tube; Move

screenshots.title: Inspect Fill parameters
screenshots.caption: Fill > Params shows the selected tube's Density, CVs per guide, Edge bias, Seed, and Length profile. The warning reflects the intentionally unfinished scalp coverage in this exercise.
screenshots.ui: Fill > Params

screenshots.title: Change guide density
screenshots.caption: The selected tube's Density is 40, with 37 guides reported in the dock. This is a partial-coverage practice scalp, not the finished character groom.
screenshots.ui: Fill > Params > Density

screenshots.title: Open Hierarchy mode
screenshots.caption: Hierarchy mode exposes Navigate, Subdivide, Merge, Group, and Levels before the selected tube is subdivided.
screenshots.ui: Hierarchy > Navigate

screenshots.title: Sculpt a guide tube
screenshots.caption: Sculpt > Grab moved the tube centers while keeping the root pinned; Brush radius reflects the F-drag resize.
screenshots.ui: Sculpt > Grab; Brush radius

screenshots.title: Build renderable hair
screenshots.caption: Output mode exposes Build hair description, Strand density multiplier, Strand width, and Show amplified hair. This practice groom still has uncovered scalp and a kink warning.
screenshots.ui: Output > Build hair description; Show amplified hair

screenshots.title: Save from the Pomade dock
screenshots.caption: The Save button is available in the Output workspace; the walkthrough next writes a .usdc groom through that button.
screenshots.ui: Save

screenshots.title: Reopen the dock
screenshots.caption: Closing and reopening the Pomade dock preserves the live scalp binding and returns to Graph mode. This is a dock reopen, not a saved-file Resume.
screenshots.ui: usdGen > Pomade > Open workspace; Graph

screenshots.title: Resume a saved groom
screenshots.caption: After reopening a scene that sublayers a saved .usdc groom, the dock offers Resume groom while no live scalp is bound.
screenshots.ui: Resume groom

screenshots.title: Saved region restored
screenshots.caption: Resume groom hydrated one tube and 27 guides on /Scalp; the saved Graph region is editable again.
screenshots.ui: Resume groom; Graph > Create region

screenshots.title: Open the stoat study
screenshots.caption: The prepared ALab stoat-groom.usda is open in usdview with HeroCam active; the Scene Graph shows Guides and Groom under /World.
screenshots.ui: Scene Graph; HeroCam

screenshots.title: Inspect the body mesh
screenshots.caption: The Scene Graph selection is the character body mesh at /World/Character/body_M_hrc/GEO/body_M_geo; the path field identifies the prim precisely.
screenshots.ui: Scene Graph > body_M_geo

screenshots.title: Inspect sparse guides
screenshots.caption: The companion stoat-guides.usda stage hides the render groom and shows the authored BasisCurves guides over the character in HeroCam.
screenshots.ui: Scene Graph > Guides; HeroCam

screenshots.title: Inspect the coat in DetailCam
screenshots.caption: DetailCam frames the stoat's head and upper coat in the live usdGen Storm viewport; the study is a prepared example scene.
screenshots.ui: DetailCam

screenshots.title: Select the coat Noise operator
screenshots.caption: With BrownBody/Ops/noise selected in usdview's Scene Graph, Noodles Editor shows the prepared operator and its magnitude value, 0.0238. The capture script exercised Add from Prim Tree (A).
screenshots.ui: usdview Scene Graph; Window > Noodles Editor; A: Add from Prim Tree
captureExercises: Scene Graph selection and A: Add from Prim Tree
Noise magnitude value-cell click, type 0.031, Enter

screenshots.title: Choose a persistent edit target
screenshots.caption: Layer Editor lists the prepared scratch layer stoat-ui-edit.usda. Clicking its row sets that persistent layer as the edit target before changing magnitude; the checked-in example remains untouched.
screenshots.ui: Window > Layer Editor; Edit Target
captureExercises: Scene Graph selection and A: Add from Prim Tree
Noise magnitude value-cell click, type 0.031, Enter

screenshots.title: Edit coat Noise magnitude
screenshots.caption: In the selected Noise node's usdGen group, a real value-cell click, typing 0.031, and Enter changed usdGen:noise:magnitude from 0.0238 to 0.031 in the scratch edit layer.
screenshots.ui: Noodles Editor; usdGen > noise:magnitude value cell
captureExercises: Scene Graph selection and A: Add from Prim Tree
Noise magnitude value-cell click, type 0.031, Enter

screenshots.title: Save the edited coat layer
screenshots.caption: After Ctrl+S in Noodles Editor, magnitude remains 0.031. The capture script verified that the selected scratch layer was saved and no longer dirty; the original scene was not rewritten.

captureExercises: Scene Graph selection and A: Add from Prim Tree
Noise magnitude value-cell click, type 0.031, Enter

screenshots.title: Scatter in Noodles Editor
screenshots.caption: Real localized Noodles Editor with Scatter selected. The density value cell is visible in its usdGen group.
screenshots.ui: Window > Noodles Editor; View > Show Attribute Values
actions: Open examples/docs/operators/scatter.usda in usdview, then choose Window > Noodles Editor (N).
In usdview's Scene Graph, select /World/Groom/Fur/Ops/scatter; focus Noodles Editor and press A to add the selected prim.
In Window > Layer Editor, choose a persistent edit target before changing a value.
Keep View > Show Attribute Values on. Right-click the Noodles canvas and choose Write Values > Default.
In the selected node's usdGen group, click the density value cell, type the value you want, and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+S in Noodles Editor to save the selected edit-target layer.
screenshots.editVerification: Per-operator edit and save steps are source-audited; the ALab Noise walkthrough exercises an actual value edit and Ctrl+S in Qt.

screenshots.title: Collide in Noodles Editor
screenshots.caption: Actual Collide node in Noodles Editor: cutThenCollide temporarily shortens deeply penetrating strands before flexible collision, with cutDepthThreshold 0.15 and cutBlendDepth 0.02 in stage units. The preset uses 128 iterations, pushAmount 1 and offset 0.
screenshots.ui: Window > Noodles Editor; View > Show Attribute Values
actions: Open examples/docs/operators/collide.usda in usdview. Choose Camera > Select Camera > CamMotion (/World/CamMotion) to frame the sphere's full descent and slide, then choose Window > Noodles Editor (N).
In usdview's Scene Graph, select /World/Groom/Fur/Ops/collide; focus Noodles Editor and press A to add the selected prim.
In Window > Layer Editor, select collide.usda as the edit target so changes and Ctrl+S preserve the sphere's existing 0, 27 and 99 motion keys in that file.
Keep View > Show Attribute Values on. Right-click the Noodles canvas and choose Write Values > Default.
In usdview select the Collide prim's usdGen:colliders relationship and inspect its two explicit targets: /World/Shield and the invisible closed /World/ScalpVolume beneath the patch.

Select /World/Shield and add it to Noodles. Its editable subdivisionScheme token is catmullClark. In usdview choose Display > Complexity > Very High to display its smooth surface; Collide uses the authored scheme independently of viewport complexity.

For a sphere motion edit, select /World/Shield in the Scene Graph and press A in Noodles. Choose Write Values > Animation (key at current frame), set Current Frame to 27, and click the Y component of xformOp:translate. The authored center is (0.5, 0.525, 0.5); change it and restore 0.525, then check frames 0 and 99 to keep all three motion keys. In the root edit layer, Ctrl+S saves the complete keyed scene.

Return Write Values to Default before editing Collide controls. At frame 27 or 99, keep offset 0, iterations 128 and resolveType flexible; click pushAmount, type 0 and press Enter to see the uncorrected fur, then type 1 and press Enter to restore native correction.

For deep contact, choose cutThenCollide with resolveType flexible, set cutDepthThreshold to 0.15 and cutBlendDepth to 0.02. Threshold is an inset from the evaluated subdivision limit; collision still bends against its outer boundary; blend controls how gradually it turns on.

With CamMotion selected, hold Current Frame at 0, 27 and 99 in turn and wait for each cook. Compare the clear, descending and sliding poses; pre-cut shortening should disappear when contact clears. For a closer settled view at frame 99, choose Camera > Select Camera > Cam (/World/Cam).

For a fur-only comparison at frame 27 or 99, open Window > Layer Editor and choose Session Layer as the edit target. Select /World/Shield in the Scene Graph, then choose Edit > Make Invisible (Ctrl+H). Wait for the hair to settle and select its visibility property to inspect the invisible value. The Shield still participates in Collide: keep both /World/Shield and /World/ScalpVolume in usdGen:colliders. Choose Edit > Remove Session Visibility (Ctrl+U) to show the sphere again, then restore your previous edit target. This inspection uses a session opinion and needs no source-layer save.

In Storm, set the timeline range to 0–99 and use the scene's 24 fps. Press Play: each frame waits for the complete current-frame groom and its converged viewport presentation, so slow cooks slow playback. Manual scrubbing remains progressive.

Press Playblast next to Play, choose an MP4 destination in the file dialog, and wait for capture and encoding. The displayed range is recorded at timeline FPS. Cancel restores the previous frame and playback state and preserves an existing output movie.
Press Ctrl+S in Noodles Editor to save the selected edit-target layer.

actions: Open examples/docs/operators/wind-clumped.usda in usdview. Choose Camera > Select Camera > Cam (/World/Cam) for the elevated view, then choose Window > Noodles Editor (N).

In Window > Layer Editor, choose a persistent edit target before changing a value.
Keep View > Show Attribute Values on. Right-click the Noodles canvas and choose Write Values > Default.

Play frames 0–99 at 24 fps. Click billowHighStrength, type 0 and press Enter to isolate broad billowing; restore 0.045 for finer ripples. Keep billowLowStrength 0.10, billowLowFrequency 0.75 and billowLowRate 0.24. Try billowHighRate 0.48, then restore 0.96, to compare ripple speed; billowHighFrequency stays 3.

For a full Wind movie, set the timeline range to 0–99 and use the scene's 24 fps. Storm Play waits for complete current-frame hair and converged viewport presentation before advancing; manual scrubbing remains progressive.

Press Playblast next to Play and choose an MP4 destination. Each ready viewport frame in the displayed range is recorded at timeline FPS even when cooking slows interactive Play. Cancel restores the previous frame and playback state and preserves an existing output movie.

Compare the matched wind-unclumped.usda scene: its /World/Groom/Fur/Ops/clump node has enabled off, while the clumped scene has it on. Both Scatter nodes author density 6500. Select those nodes to inspect the native toggle and density controls, then return to Wind.
Press Ctrl+S in Noodles Editor to save the selected edit-target layer.
